translations.text: Noah was righteous and innocent, living among those who had abandoned God.
For those who desire what is good will do it in the way they see us doing it. And those who do evil will do it in the way they see us doing it, and will go even further.

An unclean person is not merely a person who is defiled and is separated from the person who is holy. Nor is an unclean thing merely an animal that is unsuitable to offer as a sacrifice to the Lord and is separated from what is clean according to the commandments.

Rather, all evil things, from crooked judgments to hypocrisy, are unclean. Whoever touches them—that is, practices them—will become unclean before God if he does not withdraw from them, just as every sin is an impurity in the eyes of those who truly belong to God. Indeed, this is why judges who are not upright are called unclean because of their unclean deeds, while those who are upright are called clean because of their righteous deeds and their just judgments.

So too, a person who humiliates a good person, honors an evil person, and insults a righteous person in the presence of an ungodly person has an unclean heart within him, especially since he is like someone who blocks a spring of water.

Who will say that this is not so, except someone who has within him what God detests—pride—as it is written in the Gospel? Or shall we entertain these proud thoughts, I saying, “Are you the one who will guide me?” and you saying, “Is this person the one who will teach me?” Yet we have not mourned over our sins so that God will not cast us away from him on the day of our distress. Or are these not people to whom he will say at that time, “Depart from me,” or, “I do not know who you are”? What will we say at that time? Will we say, “In your name we took positions of authority or high rank; in your name we clothed ourselves in religious garments; in your name we lived in your holy places; in your name we read the Scriptures”? They too will say, “In your name we prophesied, and in your name we cast out demons, and in your name we performed many miracles.” But they will gain nothing. Why? Have they forgotten the deeds? If he will say to these people, “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire,” because they did not do what he told them, then how much more woe awaits us, because we neglect necessary deeds, namely, God's ordinances and what is right!

There is another practice that harms the fathers and brings ruin to the children: those in authority honoring people so that they will follow them, or appointing them to necessary duties in God's service, although they hear about and know their evil deeds.

There are things that a person may vow to do, or may not vow to do, namely: keeping his bed pure; giving charity if he has the means of this life; administering justice without favoritism; observing the days of fasting according to the rules of the church; and the firstfruits.

You are the one who taught him the ways of coming in and going out deceitfully. You are the one who hid him in their heart, their soul, and their thoughts, like a woman who has hidden her adulterous lover in the storerooms and
in the corners of her house.

You are the one who brought him to the place where the treasure is hidden. You are the one who pointed it out to him. Search, you foolish virgin! Go through all their possessions so that you may know what he has not taken from the things that belong to you.

Their purity is the great treasure. Prayer is the bracelets and the various rings on their hands and fingers. Their walking in freedom is the anklets on their feet. Their obedience is the earrings in their ears. Humility is the ring and the copper necklace around their neck.
Their knowledge is the ornament on their head or around their neck. Their fasts are the bridles of their body.
Grace is the ointment and the oil with which you anoint yourself and which you put on your head. Truth is the band that you tie around yourself. Wisdom is the cloth in which you wrap yourself.
How long will these troubles remain on the earth because of our acts of violence and all the things that none of us wants done to him, yet we ourselves do to one another?

But it was said, “Every matter will be established through the mouth of two or three witnesses.” Or stolen goods are found with those who took them. The end of every dispute—he said, “An oath before God shall take place between them.”

And again, “I will establish a covenant of peace with them, and a covenant of peace shall be theirs. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever. My dwelling shall be over them.”
